title: Weight Loss and Knee Arthritis: How Much Do You Really Need to Lose?
metaDescription: How much weight loss helps knee arthritis? Losing about 10% of body weight is likely better than 5%. Simple, kind advice for Indian families.
intro: Losing weight is one of the most effective things you can do for a painful knee. Every extra kilo adds strain to the knee with each step, so even a modest loss can ease pain. NICE says losing about 10% of your body weight is likely to help more than losing 5%.

sections.heading: Does weight really affect knee arthritis?
sections.body: Yes. Extra weight strains the knees, which carry your body weight with every step. Both the NHS and Versus Arthritis list being overweight as a risk factor and say a healthy weight reduces pressure on the knees.

sections.heading: How much weight should I lose?
sections.body: NICE says weight loss improves quality of life and physical function and reduces pain, and that losing 10% of body weight is likely to be better than 5%. For a person weighing 80 kg, that is about 8 kg. Any steady loss helps, so you do not need to reach an ideal number before feeling better.

sections.heading: What is the safest way to lose weight with a painful knee?
sections.body: Combine more activity with a healthier diet, as the NHS advises. Low-impact options such as swimming, water exercise and cycling are kind to the knee. Check with your doctor or physiotherapist before starting a new exercise plan. Fast crash diets are not a good idea.

sections.heading: What if I cannot exercise because of pain?
sections.body: Settle the pain first with medicines, then start gently. Even short, regular walks and chair-based leg exercises count. Food changes can start straight away, even if the knee is sore.

sections.heading: Do I have to lose weight before knee replacement?
sections.body: Not always. We discuss your own situation at your visit, and no one should feel judged about weight.

faqs.q: How much weight loss reduces knee pain?
faqs.a: Losing about 10% of body weight is likely to help more than 5%, according to NICE.

faqs.q: Is weight loss better than injections for knee arthritis?
faqs.a: They do different jobs. Weight loss treats a cause of strain; injections only ease pain for a time.

faqs.q: Can I treat knee arthritis only with diet?
faqs.a: Diet helps through weight loss. No specific food has been shown to cure arthritis. Versus Arthritis says body weight is a bigger factor than any particular food.

faqs.q: How fast should I lose weight?
faqs.a: Slow and steady is safer. A dietitian or your doctor can help set a plan.

faqs.q: Will losing weight make arthritis go away?
faqs.a: It does not cure it, but it can reduce pain and improve how you move.
